Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay, good morning everyone, thanks for carving time, um we wanted to go over where the SDK hooks landed and the structured output contract you folks sketched out last week — hi Priya, hi Marco.
[00:12] Priya: hi Maya, hey Liam. Morning. We've got the basic SDK calls wired in, function calling mapping is, like, functional but there are a few spots where the model returns unexpected keys.
[00:22] Liam: yeah that's what we saw in the last run, the function-calling envelope from the runtime sometimes returns a different casing — like "toolResult" vs "tool_result" — and that breaks a strict JSON schema.
[00:33] Marco: yeah we hit it when we tried to deserialize into our typed structs, whole pipeline crashed for some requests.
[00:38] Maya: ok noted. Priya can you show the sample schema you mentioned? or drop it in the thread after?
[00:44] Priya: I'll drop. It's minimal: action (string), args (object), confidence (float), and items (array of objects). But we have nested arrays and sometimes the model emits an empty string instead of null, or returns a top-level note that isn't in the schema.
[00:58] Shelly: from security side we also need an explicit field that indicates whether the response touched PII-sensitive KB or not. So a small meta flag would help us route on-prem vs hosted.
[01:10] Jae: and the SREs want a consistent request_id and model_variant in the telemetry so we can trace. We couldn't correlate some of the invocations to the agent logs.
[01:20] Liam: totally — the SDK can attach request_id, model_variant, and we can include it in the response envelope as a header. The only caveat is if you do function-calling and external tools, sometimes the tool output comes asynchronously and we end up with nested partials.
[01:33] Priya: that was one of our issues — we call the billing-tool via a function call, and sometimes it returns a markdown blob unexpectedly.
[01:40] Maya: ok, let's enumerate the failure modes: casing/key variance, empty-string vs null, nested arrays inconsistent shape, and tool outputs not matching declared types. Anything else?
[01:51] Marco: model hallucinating extra fields like "estimated_cost" when we never asked for it — then our serializer chokes.
[01:58] Liam: for that one we usually recommend a post-validation layer — the SDK has a validateResponse(schema) helper that returns a list of mismatches. You can run that before ingestion.
[02:08] Priya: we saw validateResponse but it adds 60-80ms on the call path which is annoying for low-latency flows.
[02:15] Liam: yeah there's a tradeoff. We can recommend offloading heavy schema-checking to async workers for synchronous requests where latency matters. Or we can provide a minimal fast-path check that only validates top-level keys.
[02:27] Shelly: from a security/forensics POV we also want the raw unvalidated payload to be stored for audit, but redaction applied before retention. Is that supported?
[02:36] Maya: yes, Redwood has a configurable retention pipeline — we can capture raw payloads to a private bucket and apply redaction rules before longer-term storage, that is doable in Private or Dedicated setups.
[02:49] Jae: quick Q — if we run on your hosted tier, where does the raw capture live? We need to ensure it stays in the region for data residency.
[02:57] Maya: good question — hosted has region pins; raw captures can be stored in customer-specified region for enterprise customers, otherwise default to region of the endpoint. For strict residency you may want Dedicated or Private.
[03:10] Priya: ok on to latency — Liam you ran the 1k token bench last week, results were promising, can you summarize?
[03:17] Liam: yes. With batching disabled and KV cache cold we saw mean p50 ~ 230ms for 1k prefix tokens, p95 ~ 420ms. With prefix caching warmed and our continuous batching off, p50 drops to ~120ms. But the heavier failure mode is tail when sequence lengths spike.
[03:34] Marco: what's the expected tail for 2k? I think our flows sometimes hit 1.8k.
[03:40] Liam: for 2k we expect p95 in the 600-900ms range depending on quantization mode — floatt16 vs int8. We can run the exact numbers for your prompt distribution.
[03:50] Priya: can you run one with quantized model + no batching + KV cache enabled? That's closest to our production target.
[03:58] Liam: yeah we'll do that as an action item — run 2k steady-state bench with KV cache and quantized model. I'll add the bench sheet link. (link posted)
[04:08] Marco: also curious about function-calling cost — do we get charged per tool call or per token?
[04:14] Maya: per-token pricing applies to model tokens; tool calls that are external don't add model tokens unless the model generates them. There can be operational egress costs for tool execution but model usage is per-token. We'll send a pricing example for typical function-call heavy flows.
[04:26] Shelly: security question: we need SOC2 attestation and KMS/HSM integration for key material. Are those available in the POC?
[04:34] Maya: SOC2 reports we can provide to sign NDA'd legal review; KMS integration is available on Dedicated and Private; on hosted we support customer-managed keys for certain enterprise tiers. We'll surface the security one-pager.
[04:46] Jae: another SRE point — when you do rolling model rollouts, do you provide a traffic-splitting API so we can do canary at 5%?
[04:55] Liam: yes, the rollout API supports % traffic splits plus automatic fallback to the previous version on error rate spikes. It also supports per-route pinning.
[05:03] Priya: back to structured output — we will produce canonical schema today and include 5 failing examples. Also we have edge cases where the model returns a top-level string instead of JSON object when it times out. How should we handle that?
[05:16] Liam: typical approach is wrapper parsing: first attempt to parse as JSON, if parse fails, run a 1-shot repair prompt through the model to extract structured content, or fail-safe to async worker which triggers a human-loop.
[05:28] Marco: repair prompts seem risky in regulated flow, might be better to fail closed and route to manual review.
[05:34] Shelly: yes we have compliance constraints, manual review is acceptable for some categories but we need metadata flags to triage.
[05:41] Maya: so agreed — we'll add a small metadata field "validation_state": ["ok","repair_attempted","manual_review_required"], and SDK will emit these states.
[05:51] Priya: that would help. Also can the SDK emit a small "schema_diff" array with at most 3 mismatches to keep payload small?
[05:59] Liam: yes we can provide a compact diff. It's currently a verbose list but we can add a compact mode. That's a small change.
[06:07] Marco: timeline wise, if we get bench numbers and schema this week can we aim to have a production-mirroring pilot in the dedicated pool by end of month?
[06:16] Maya: that's plausible — depends on signatures and security review, but technically we can spin a dedicated pool and run a soak test in 3-5 business days once contract is live.
[06:26] Priya: on contract — are there any minimums for Dedicated?
[06:29] Maya: yes there's a monthly committed throughput baseline for Dedicated; I'll send examples for small, medium, and large tiers. We can also do a short-term trial with usage-based billing that converts to reserved capacity later.
[06:40] Shelly: legal will probably ask for a data processing addendum and an audit SOC2 copy.
[06:44] Maya: understood, I'll attach the DPA template and SOC2 redacted report to the thread after the call.
[06:52] Jae: quick note — we need the telemetry fields list so our instrumentation can pick up the right metrics.
[06:57] Maya: I'll get that to you — Liam, can you draft an event spec?
[07:01] Liam: yes will do.
[07:03] Priya: ok final quick ask — for function-calling, when the tool returns non-JSON, can the SDK attempt to coerce into the declared type and include original tool output in a debug field? That helps dev productivity.
[07:15] Liam: yes we'll offer an optional "coerce_and_debug" flag that includes the rawToolOutput under debug.raw_tool. It's off by default.
[07:24] Marco: perfect. That's it from us.
[07:27] Maya: recap: action items as discussed — Liam run 2k bench with KV cache + quant, prepare compact schema_diff, and event spec; Priya share canonical schema and failing examples; Maya share pricing + DPA + SOC2 link; Shelly confirm security asks and list; Jae provide telemetry needs. Next sync Thursday 2026-03-18 09:30 PT.
